question.text: Liquidity risk is typically measured using:

answer.text: Bid-ask spread and time to execute without price impact

explanation.text: The Logic: The source describes liquidity risk as being determined by the bid-ask spread and the time required to execute the trade without impacting price. The bid-ask spread itself is treated as the cost of unwinding a position. The Trap: VaR alone, Sharpe ratio and beta describe return-distribution or systematic-risk concepts and do not capture the cost and time dimensions of liquidity. Note: Both dimensions — spread and execution time — should be considered together when assessing position liquidity.
